_tier1_note: Tier 1 allow rules. Operator ruling 2026-08-13: 'battery commands to Tier 1
via item-27 amendment; post-merge cleandown granted for self-refusing forms
only (-d, --ff-only, --prune)'.
TWO STANDING CONSTRAINTS govern every addition here.
(1) A Tier 1 allow rule PRE-EMPTS a Tier 2 guard ask (tested 2026-08-11).
The two are alternatives, not layers, so never grant here anything the
governance guard is relied on to gate. Nothing below is protected-path or
state-dependent.
(2) Never allow-list a command family carrying a DENY, since whether a deny
is pre-empted the same way is untested and has no safe probe.
REPO_MANIFEST IS DELIBERATELY NARROWED, not widened: only the --out form is
granted. The bare invocation writes REPO_MANIFEST.md into the tree, which is
the F6 divergence closed at CL-27, and it must keep prompting so the
superseded form cannot be reached without a deliberate confirmation.
GIT BRANCH -d IS LOWERCASE ONLY. -D force-deletes an unmerged branch and is
NOT granted. See the open risk recorded in the PR body: whether the matcher
folds case is unestablished, so the -d/-D boundary is asserted here but not
yet proven.
AMENDMENT 2 (2026-08-13, NARROWED). Ruled: 'read-class Bash families widened
to Tier 1 ... precedence probe series runs first and gates the widening'. The
probe series RAN and returned UNPROVABLE, not proven: adding a matching allow
rule for a denied command, probing, and removing it produced an IDENTICAL
refusal in all three states. Two hypotheses fit equally - deny beats allow, or
settings.json does not reload mid-session - and they cannot be separated from
inside the harness, because the discriminator is whether a PROMPT fired and
prompts are not observable here. The ruling's UNPROVABLE branch therefore
applies: only ZERO-DENY-OVERLAP families land. Two did.
GRANTED: verification heredocs (the PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python read/hash/
report construction), Bash only - PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix, so
the same pattern is not expressible there and no PowerShell twin is added.
GRANTED: gh READS only - pr view, pr checks, pr list, pr diff. Structurally
distinct from gh pr merge, which stays at the guard under the Option B gate.
DEFERRED BY NAME, and these return only when precedence is PROVEN at the
operator's terminal: all git-family read grants beyond those already present
(push overlap makes the deny-precedence question load-bearing); filesystem
reads (ls beyond the existing grant, find, stat); text search (grep, rg);
text slicing (head, tail, wc, cut, sort). Each is low risk on its face and
each is excluded anyway, because the ruled branch is zero-overlap only and
'low risk' is not the test.
NOT GRANTED, EVER, under this amendment: any wildcard over a command family
(Bash(python:*), Bash(git:*), Bash(gh:*)). A wildcard would silently cover
write-class members whose only protection is a deny whose precedence is now
formally unknown.
SYSTEM PROPERTY discovered while authoring this: a Bash command CANNOT write
a permission rule naming a denied command, because the rule text contains the
command and the guard matches the command string. The Edit path is the
designed route - the guard gates it by PATH with an ask, not by content.
